why, and where it would go: cd.cuh:164-166 constructs std::mt19937 g(rand()) and then initShuffle reseeds it with random_state = 0; each epoch calls std::shuffle(ri, g). The C++ standard does not specify std::shuffle's algorithm (libstdc++'s __gen_two_uniform_ints packs two draws per swap when the range allows; libc++ draws one per swap), so the permutation is a function of the toolchain, not of the seed alone, and cannot be gated bitwise or certified across vendors. An exact port = mt19937 (fully specified) + libstdc++'s std::shuffle transcribed and NAMED as the algorithm, gated by a permutation-is-a-pure-function-of-the-seed check = DEVIATION 611, reserved and not spent. Would go in solver/impl/solver/shuffle.mojo beside init_shuffle
